newsitem.title: INDIA: Northeast India to halt tea output to end-March.
newsitem.headline: Northeast India to halt tea output to end-March.

text.p: Planters in northeastern India will halt tea production to end-March to maintain market quality, a Tea Association of India (TAI) official said on Thursday.
"We have decided to stop production as soon as winter sets in this month so that only quality teas are provided to the market," N.C. Baruah, secretary general of TAI's Assam branch, told Reuters.
Baruah said planters in Assam and Darjeeling would stop producing teas in phases from November so that there was no carry-forward of bad quality tea to next year.
Production in the two areas is expected to begin in end-March or early April.
"What we intend to do is that the market gets only quality teas because leaves harden in winter season and there is a seasonal decline in production," Baruah said.
He said in such situations some unscrupulous traders might sell poor quality teas affecting prices.
Baruah said India's tea output was growing. According to available trends this year, production was forecast to be 35 to 40 million kg more than 1995 production of 753 million kg, he said.
In 1994, planters in Darjeeling and Assam also stopped tea production to maintain quality.
